questions.title: Overidentified linear IV: efficient GMM, reproduction and inference
questions.description: Develop a complete source-assisted known-result research analysis of overidentified linear instrumental-variable estimation with independent observations and potentially heteroskedastic errors. Regressors may be endogenous. In persistent Markdown/LaTeX, state explicit identification, rank, moment and weighting conditions; derive consistency, the asymptotic linear representation and limiting covariance for a general positive-definite GMM weight; establish optimal weighting within this class; justify feasible two-step estimation and its sampling covariance; and derive the null asymptotic distribution and degrees of freedom of the efficient overidentification statistic. Distinguish missing assumptions, exact finite-sample identities and asymptotic conclusions, including the consequences of invalid or weak instruments. Reproduce the pinned linearmodels 7.0 IV example through its two-step GMM fit and the declared unchanged upstream tests, preserving actual data, environment and output identity. Explain what that example does and does not establish about causal validity and the theory. Implement the public estimator interface using model-authored Python with disclosed numerical-library reuse. Use exploratory computation to challenge the derivations and implementation, then obtain independent review of the exact current theory and source. Freeze and execute confirmation in at least two nondegenerate strong-identification designs, one homoskedastic and one heteroskedastic, each with at least 1000 independent datasets. Assess coefficient bias, nominal 95 percent interval coverage, estimated-versus-empirical covariance, nominal 5 percent overidentification-test rejection and numerical failures; both coverage and rejection-rate Monte Carlo standard errors must be at most 0.01. Freeze seeds, criteria, precision and stopping before outcomes, and report all unmet criteria. Bind source reproduction, current mathematical derivations, generated code, review and actual confirmation into the final research report. This is an iid linear specialization of the GMM theory, not the entire stationary-dependent theory of Hansen (1982), blind rediscovery, novel causal identification, or a claim that the observed empirical instruments are valid. Formalization is not required.

source.primary_authority: Lars Peter Hansen (1982), Large Sample Properties of Generalized Method of Moments Estimators, Econometrica 50(4), 1029-1054, DOI 10.2307/1912775. The task concerns its iid linear overidentified specialization. Public computational reproduction uses linearmodels 7.0 at 28af72ed08b1df00157d08a12a16a6c18f31a358 and the MEPS example, not original-paper experiments.

request_fields.name: x
request_fields.edge_cases: Any intercept or exogenous covariate is an explicit supplied column; do not append an intercept.
request_fields.meaning: All regressors, including any endogenous and exogenous regressors, in their intended coefficient order.

request_fields.name: z
request_fields.shape: Finite n-by-q matrix, p<q<=p+4 and n>q+p.
request_fields.indexing: Same observation order as x, then instrument.
request_fields.edge_cases: Includes all intended instruments, including any intercept or exogenous regressor used as its own instrument. Evaluated design cross moments have full identification rank and required covariance matrices are positive definite and well-conditioned.
request_fields.meaning: The complete instrument matrix; do not substitute the endogenous regressor for its instruments.

request_fields.name: y
request_fields.indexing: Same observation order as x and z.
request_fields.meaning: Observed independent responses in a linear structural regression with valid population instrument moments.

response_fields.name: coefficients
response_fields.edge_cases: Exactly two steps: the first weight is the inverse uncentered sample second moment of z; the second is the inverse uncentered instrument-score second moment evaluated at first-step residuals. Do not use an iterated or continuously updating estimator.
response_fields.meaning: Two-step heteroskedastic GMM coefficient estimate with no regularization.
response_fields.normalization: Original supplied coordinates; sample moments are observation averages.

response_fields.name: covariance
response_fields.shape: Finite symmetric p-by-p matrix on convergence.
response_fields.edge_cases: Use the full robust sandwich with the same second-step weight and instrument-score second moment at the returned coefficients. Scores are uncentered; no degrees-of-freedom adjustment. This is the linearmodels robust, debiased=False convention.
response_fields.meaning: Feasible sampling covariance of the returned coefficients, not the covariance of their square-root-n limit or a matrix of standard errors.
response_fields.normalization: Sampling covariance includes one factor of 1/n.

response_fields.name: j_statistic
response_fields.shape: Finite nonnegative scalar up to numerical roundoff.
response_fields.edge_cases: Evaluate the second-step quadratic moment criterion at the returned coefficients, using that step's weight, not an unweighted residual sum of squares.
response_fields.meaning: Efficient overidentification statistic, normalized as n times the quadratic criterion formed from average moments.
response_fields.normalization: One factor of n outside the average-moment quadratic form.

response_fields.name: j_degrees_of_freedom
response_fields.edge_cases: Count all supplied regressor and instrument columns, including intercepts.
response_fields.meaning: Number of overidentifying moment restrictions under the stated full-rank model.

response_fields.name: converged
response_fields.edge_cases: Report singular or unresolved numerical work honestly, not as a successful fit.
response_fields.meaning: Whether the requested fit and covariance are numerically resolved.
response_fields.normalization: Numerical status only, not statistical correctness.

invariants.meaning: Do not mutate the request or use undeclared external data. NumPy/SciPy numerical reuse is permitted; source and its configuration remain model-owned. Extra response fields are allowed.

Every result describes the same supplied sample. Joint row permutations preserve estimates. Nonsingular instrument-coordinate transformations leave estimates, covariance and J unchanged. Rescaling a regressor changes its coefficient and covariance in the corresponding inverse coordinates without changing fitted responses or J.

Only valid numerically resolvable requests are evaluated. No undeclared malformed-input, coercion, solver-choice or exact floating-point equality test is imposed; results are compared with numerical tolerances.

empirical_claims.meaning: Freeze at least two strong-identification valid-instrument designs, one homoskedastic and one heteroskedastic, with at least 1000 independent samples per design; freeze seeds, precision, criteria and stopping before confirmation. Rate MCSE must be <=0.01.
Assess bias, nominal 95 percent coefficient coverage, empirical-versus-estimated covariance, nominal 5 percent null J-test rejection and numerical failures on the exact current implementation.

Justify each design's validity, endogeneity, rank and heteroskedasticity assumptions. Report unmet criteria and limitations; asymptotic laws do not give exact finite-sample calibration, and reproduction does not prove real-data instrument validity.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: Finite-dimensional numerical linear algebra with honest status; no prescribed reasoning length, scratch count or revision sequence.
